::: {.route-question}
Question for today: CellCo's cell line is running, slow or down in every shift. How much of the time will it run, and is the night shift really worse?
:::

## A line that changes state {#states}

::: {.two}
::: {}
Every shift, CellCo records the state of the cell line: **Running (R)**, **Slow (S)** or **Down (D)**.

A **Markov chain** assumes the next state depends only on the current state, not on the history before it.

The transition matrix *P* holds the probability of moving from each state (row) to each state (column). Each row sums to 1.
:::
::: {}
```{=html}
<table class="wide">
  <thead><tr><th>From \ To</th><th class="num">R</th><th class="num">S</th><th class="num">D</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td>Running</td><td class="num">4/6</td><td class="num">1/6</td><td class="num">1/6</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Slow</td><td class="num">3/6</td><td class="num">2/6</td><td class="num">1/6</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Down</td><td class="num">3/6</td><td class="num">1/6</td><td class="num">2/6</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
```
[The probabilities are sixths so that a die can play the line in Activity 1.]{.hint}
:::
:::

## Where will the line be in *n* shifts? {#n-step}

```{=html}
<div class="formula"><p>π<sub><i>n</i></sub> = π<sub>0</sub> · <i>P</i><sup><i>n</i></sup> &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; steady state: π = π<i>P</i>, Σ π<sub><i>i</i></sub> = 1</p></div>
<table class="wide">
  <thead><tr><th>Start in Down</th><th class="num">P(R)</th><th class="num">P(S)</th><th class="num">P(D)</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td>After 1 shift</td><td class="num">0.500</td><td class="num">0.167</td><td class="num">0.333</td></tr>
    <tr><td>After 2 shifts</td><td class="num">0.583</td><td class="num">0.194</td><td class="num">0.222</td></tr>
    <tr><td>After 4 shifts</td><td class="num">0.600</td><td class="num">0.200</td><td class="num">0.201</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Steady state π</td><td class="num hit">0.600</td><td class="num">0.200</td><td class="num">0.200</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
```

[After about four shifts the line forgets where it started. In the long run it runs 60% of shifts. If a slow shift makes half the cells, throughput is 0.6 + 0.5 × 0.2 = 70% of capacity.]{.note-line}

## Watch the chain forget {#n-explorer data-hold="true"}

```{=html}
<div class="widget" id="nx">
  <div class="w-controls">
    <span class="w-toggle" role="group" aria-label="Start state"><button type="button" data-st="0" aria-pressed="false">Start Running</button><button type="button" data-st="1" aria-pressed="false">Start Slow</button><button type="button" data-st="2" aria-pressed="true">Start Down</button></span>
    <label class="w-slider">Shifts <i>n</i> <strong id="nx-nv">1</strong><input type="range" id="nx-n" min="0" max="10" step="1" value="1"></label>
  </div>
  <svg id="nx-svg" viewBox="0 0 1160 230" role="img" aria-label="Probability of each state after n shifts, compared with the steady state"></svg>
  <div class="w-readout" id="nx-out" aria-live="polite"></div>
</div>
<script>
(function () {
  const root = document.getElementById('nx'); if (!root) return;
  root.addEventListener('click', (e) => e.stopPropagation());
  const P = [[4/6, 1/6, 1/6], [3/6, 2/6, 1/6], [3/6, 1/6, 2/6]], pi = [0.6, 0.2, 0.2];
  const names = ['Running', 'Slow', 'Down'], cols = ['#0F6E6B', '#E29A2D', '#BE654C'];
  let st = 2;
  function draw() {
    const n = +document.getElementById('nx-n').value; document.getElementById('nx-nv').textContent = n;
    let v = [0, 0, 0]; v[st] = 1;
    for (let k = 0; k < n; k++) v = [0, 1, 2].map((j) => v.reduce((s, x, i) => s + x * P[i][j], 0));
    const L = 200, W = 1160, X = (p) => L + p * (W - L - 120);
    let g = '';
    for (const p of [0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1]) g += `<line x1="${X(p)}" x2="${X(p)}" y1="6" y2="200" stroke="#B9C1C6"/><text x="${X(p)}" y="222" text-anchor="middle" font-size="16" fill="#333F4A">${p}</text>`;
    names.forEach((nm, i) => {
      const y = 14 + i * 64;
      g += `<text x="${L - 14}" y="${y + 30}" text-anchor="end" font-size="20" fill="#1C242B">${nm}</text>`;
      g += `<rect x="${X(0)}" y="${y + 8}" width="${X(v[i]) - X(0)}" height="34" fill="${cols[i]}" opacity=".85"/>`;
      g += `<line x1="${X(pi[i])}" x2="${X(pi[i])}" y1="${y}" y2="${y + 50}" stroke="#1C242B" stroke-width="2.5" stroke-dasharray="5 4"/>`;
      g += `<text x="${X(v[i]) + 8}" y="${y + 31}" font-size="18" fill="#1C242B">${v[i].toFixed(3)}</text>`;
    });
    document.getElementById('nx-svg').innerHTML = g;
    const gap = Math.max(...v.map((x, i) => Math.abs(x - pi[i])));
    document.getElementById('nx-out').innerHTML = `After ${n} shift${n === 1 ? '' : 's'}: largest distance from the steady state (dashed lines) is <b>${gap.toFixed(3)}</b>.`;
  }
  root.querySelectorAll('[data-st]').forEach((b) => b.addEventListener('click', () => { st = +b.dataset.st; root.querySelectorAll('[data-st]').forEach((x) => x.setAttribute('aria-pressed', x === b)); draw(); }));
  document.getElementById('nx-n').addEventListener('input', draw);
  draw();
})();
</script>
```

## Two quick readings of π {#readings}

::: {.takeaways}
::: {.tk}
**Mean recurrence time.** The line returns to Down every 1/π~D~ = 1/0.2 = **5 shifts** on average.
:::
::: {.tk}
**Mean run length.** Once running, it stays running for 1/(1 − 4/6) = **3 shifts** on average.
:::
::: {.tk .key}
**Capacity planning.** At 70% effective throughput, a line rated 2 GWh/yr delivers about 1.4 GWh/yr. This links directly to the demand numbers in Sessions 1 to 3.
:::
:::

## Activity 1 · Dice Markov chain {#act1 .activity data-hold="true"}

[Whole class, then pairs · 25 minutes · one die each]{.act-label}

::: {.prompt}
You are the cell line. Start in Running and roll your die ten times, writing down your state after each roll.
:::

1. From R: 1 to 4 → R, 5 → S, 6 → D. From S: 1 to 3 → R, 4 and 5 → S, 6 → D. From D: 1 to 3 → R, 4 → S, 5 and 6 → D.
2. Count your transitions (R→R, R→S, ...) and add them to the table on the board.
3. In pairs, estimate each transition probability from the class total. How close is it to the true sixths?
4. What share of all recorded shifts was Running? Compare with 0.6.

::: {.selfstudy}
Studying alone: roll 30 times and estimate the Running row.
:::

## Estimating *P* from a log {#estimate}

```{=html}
<div class="formula"><p>p̂<sub><i>ij</i></sub> = <i>n</i><sub><i>ij</i></sub> / <i>n</i><sub><i>i</i></sub> &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; SE = √( p̂<sub><i>ij</i></sub>(1 − p̂<sub><i>ij</i></sub>) / <i>n</i><sub><i>i</i></sub> ) &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; 95% interval ≈ p̂ ± 1.96 SE</p></div>
```

::: {.two}
::: {}
Count the moves out of each state, then divide by the row total. This is the maximum-likelihood estimate.

The day shift's log has 635 moves out of Running, 448 of them to Running: p̂~RR~ = 0.706, SE 0.018, so the 95% interval is **0.67 to 0.74**.
:::
::: {}
::: {.route-question}
A row with few visits has a wide interval. Down was visited only 189 times by day, so its row has an SE of about 0.035, twice that of the Running row.
:::
:::
:::

## How much data do you need? {#sample-explorer data-hold="true"}

```{=html}
<div class="widget" id="sx">
  <div class="w-controls">
    <label class="w-slider">Shifts logged <strong id="sx-nv">300</strong><input type="range" id="sx-n" min="0" max="6" step="1" value="2"></label>
    <button type="button" class="w-btn" id="sx-go">Draw a new log</button>
  </div>
  <table class="wide" id="sx-t"></table>
  <div class="w-readout" id="sx-out" aria-live="polite"></div>
</div>
<script>
(function () {
  const root = document.getElementById('sx'); if (!root) return;
  root.addEventListener('click', (e) => e.stopPropagation());
  const P = [[4/6, 1/6, 1/6], [3/6, 2/6, 1/6], [3/6, 1/6, 2/6]], Ns = [30, 100, 300, 1000, 3000, 10000, 30000], nm = ['R', 'S', 'D'];
  let seed = 3;
  const rnd = () => { seed = (seed * 16807) % 2147483647; return seed / 2147483647; };
  function draw() {
    const N = Ns[+document.getElementById('sx-n').value]; document.getElementById('sx-nv').textContent = N.toLocaleString('en-US');
    const C = [[0, 0, 0], [0, 0, 0], [0, 0, 0]]; let s = 0;
    for (let k = 0; k < N; k++) { const u = rnd(); let t = 0, c = P[s][0]; while (u > c && t < 2) { t++; c += P[s][t]; } C[s][t]++; s = t; }
    let rows = '', worst = 0;
    C.forEach((r, i) => {
      const n = r[0] + r[1] + r[2];
      rows += `<tr><td>From ${nm[i]} (n = ${n})</td>` + r.map((x, j) => {
        const p = n ? x / n : 0, h = n ? 1.96 * Math.sqrt(p * (1 - p) / n) : 1; worst = Math.max(worst, h);
        return `<td class="num">${p.toFixed(3)} ± ${h.toFixed(3)}</td>`; }).join('') + `<td class="num">${P[i].map((x) => (x * 6).toFixed(0) + '/6').join(', ')}</td></tr>`;
    });
    document.getElementById('sx-t').innerHTML = '<thead><tr><th>Estimated row</th><th class="num">to R</th><th class="num">to S</th><th class="num">to D</th><th class="num">True</th></tr></thead><tbody>' + rows + '</tbody>';
    document.getElementById('sx-out').innerHTML = `Widest 95% half-width: <b>±${worst.toFixed(3)}</b>. Ten times more data makes the interval about √10 ≈ 3.2 times narrower.`;
  }
  document.getElementById('sx-n').addEventListener('input', draw);
  document.getElementById('sx-go').addEventListener('click', draw);
  draw();
})();
</script>
```

## Is the night shift different? {#homogeneity}

```{=html}
<table class="wide">
  <thead><tr><th>1,000 shifts each</th><th class="num">R→R</th><th class="num">R→S</th><th class="num">R→D</th><th class="num">S→R</th><th class="num">S→S</th><th class="num">S→D</th><th class="num">D→R</th><th class="num">D→S</th><th class="num">D→D</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td>Day</td><td class="num">448</td><td class="num">92</td><td class="num">95</td><td class="num">88</td><td class="num">60</td><td class="num">28</td><td class="num">99</td><td class="num">24</td><td class="num">66</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Night</td><td class="num">315</td><td class="num">91</td><td class="num hit">122</td><td class="num">92</td><td class="num">73</td><td class="num">41</td><td class="num">121</td><td class="num">42</td><td class="num">103</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
```

::: {.two}
::: {}
For each row, a chi-square test compares day and night (2 × 3 table, 2 degrees of freedom). The three tests add up:

χ² = 16.85 + 1.46 + 2.24 = **20.55**, df = 6, p = **0.002**.
:::
::: {}
::: {.route-question}
One matrix does not fit both shifts. The difference sits in the Running row: by night, a running line breaks down in 23% of shifts, against 15% by day.
:::
:::
:::

## Activity 2 · Day or night? {#act2 .activity data-hold="true"}

[Pairs · 15 minutes · calculator]{.act-label}

::: {.prompt}
Use the day and night counts on the previous slide.
:::

1. Estimate p̂~RD~ for day and for night, with 95% intervals. Do the intervals overlap?
2. If the night line behaved like the day line, how many more shifts per 1,000 would it run? Use the steady state of each matrix.
3. Write one sentence for the plant manager: what should the night shift investigate first?

[Night Running row: 315, 91, 122 out of 528. Day Running row: 448, 92, 95 out of 635.]{.hint}

::: {.selfstudy}
Studying alone: answer question 1, then check it on the next slide.
:::

## Activity 2 · Answer {#act2-answer}

::: {.two}
::: {}
Day: p̂~RD~ = 95/635 = 0.150 ± 0.028. Night: 122/528 = 0.231 ± 0.036. The intervals do not overlap.

Steady-state share of Running: day matrix **0.635**, night matrix **0.528**. Matching the day shift would add about **107 running shifts per 1,000**.
:::
::: {}
::: {.route-question}
Investigate why running night shifts break down: maintenance handover, staffing, or the start-up after a planned stop. The Slow and Down rows do not differ significantly.
:::
:::
:::

## What we learned {#debrief}

::: {.takeaways}
::: {.tk}
A Markov chain is a transition matrix. π~n~ = π~0~P^n^, and the steady state solves π = πP. CellCo's line runs 60% of shifts in the long run.
:::
::: {.tk}
Estimate each row as counts divided by visits, and report its interval. Rarely visited states have the widest intervals.
:::
::: {.tk .key}
Test whether one matrix fits all conditions before you use it. CellCo's night shift breaks down more often, χ² = 20.6 with p = 0.002.
:::
:::
